name: manual_90cf6d
claim: With parallel read-only analysts, give each a distinct lens and brief it fully, then let ONE writer apply every edit sequentially; analysts diversify findings, and a single writer means shared files are never written concurrently. It does not prevent merge conflicts when separate commits are later integrated: resolve those as a union, then re-run tests and a mutation check.

decisions.notes: Narrows the superseded claim to concurrent writes: a single writer prevents concurrent edits to shared files but not merge conflicts when separate commits are integrated, as PT#450 review noted and the same day's cherry-pick union conflict showed.

rationale: Narrows the superseded claim to concurrent writes: a single writer prevents concurrent edits to shared files but not merge conflicts when separate commits are integrated, as PT#450 review noted and the same day's cherry-pick union conflict showed.
